gmdn.gmdnPTDefinition: An implantable disk-like device intended to be used for the minimally-invasive closure of cardiac defects and deployed using a dedicated delivery catheter/sheath. It is made of wire mesh [e.g., nickel-titanium alloy (Nitinol)], and possibly additional materials (e.g., polyester), and is typically self-expandable. The device is used to treat cardiac disorders that may include (but not limited to) atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), patent foramen ovale (PFO), or patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Disposable devices dedicated to implantation may be included with the implant.

productCodes.definition: Closure of clinically significant leak associated with a permanently implanted cardiac device
productCodes.physicalState: implant is typically comprised of standard permanent implant medical device materials such as metals and/or non-resorbable polymers.
productCodes.targetArea: the space between an implanted device and native tissue
productCodes.technicalMethod: permanent implant placed percutaneously (transcatheter approach) in the defect causing the leak
